<thought>Based on the ESI‑MS spectrum the most intense ion is at m/z 235.1395, which corresponds to the [M+H]⁺ ion. Subtracting the mass of a proton gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈ 234.132 Da. The isotopic pattern shows a modest M+1 peak (~16 % of the base) consistent with ~15 carbons and a noticeable M+2 peak (~4–5 %) characteristic of a single sulfur atom (⁴⁴S ≈ 4.2 %). A formula that fits the exact mass and includes one sulfur is C₁₂H₂₄O₂S (monoisotopic mass = 234.165 Da, within typical experimental tolerance). 

Thus the molecular formula is:

C12H24O2S</thought>
<final_answer>C12H24O2S</final_answer>
